missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-huber-robust-location-C007 (partial): The success-condition element 'preserve the identified source variants' is not met. Huber 1964, Sec. 4, Example (iii) (printed p.79, inside the cited Secs. 1-7) says two things about t_0 = T_n(x). First, observations with |x_i - t_0| > k may be replaced by t_0 +- k 'without changing the estimate T_n(x)'. Second, t_0 is then the arithmetic mean of the modified sample. The entry keeps only the second claim, plus the statement that the score still vanishes at t_0 (huber-robust-location.tex body lines 145-147). The annex (lines 191-194) proves only that t_0 still minimizes the modified criterion, and it adds that the replacement 'need not preserve every tie-breaking rule for every modified sample'. Neither the body nor the annex states or proves that the defined estimate T_{n,k} of the modified sample equals T_{n,k}(x); that would need a proof that t_0 is the unique zero of the modified score. No other file on the reader route supplies it either. The source's estimate-invariance claim is therefore neither kept nor explicitly corrected, and the annex hedge leaves its status unsettled. The finite computation, the mean identity and both worked examples are fully supplied.

sections.title: Huber's location estimation and least-favorable constructions

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-huber-robust-location-C003 (partial): Source variant not preserved, and no worked boundary. The entry calls itself the source's Lemmas 2--3 (handbook/parts/p15/huber-robust-location.tex line 60). It omits the source's Remark to Lemma 3 (Huber 1964, printed p.77, PDF p.5). That Remark lets the sign-change hypothesis on lambda be replaced by a weaker one: lambda exists and is finite at some xi_0 and does not vanish identically on a nondegenerate interval. Neither body 49-62 nor annex 46-83 states or derives this alternative hypothesis. The boundary it marks (lambda vanishing on an interval, where minimizing choices need not converge) is not worked. A grep finds the variant nowhere else in P15.

ED26-P15-CH-huber-robust-location-C007 (partial): Source variant narrowed. The source's Winsorizing property (example (iii), printed p.79, PDF p.7) takes t_0 = T_n(x). It replaces each observation with |x_i - t_0| > k by the nearer of t_0 - k and t_0 + k, without changing the estimate T_n(x), and t_0 equals the modified mean. The entry (body 145-147) states only that, for any zero t_0, the score still vanishes at t_0 and t_0 is the modified mean. The annex (188-194) proves only that a minimizing location is preserved. It adds that the replacement 'need not preserve every tie-breaking rule for every modified sample'. The invariance of the estimate itself is neither stated nor proved: the modified sample's zero set is the single point t_0, so its midpoint estimate equals T_{n,k}(x).

ED26-P15-CH-huber-robust-location-C013 (partial): Source variant narrowed: a promised case is missing. The source (Sec. 7, printed p.83, PDF p.11) says the bias bound is reached whenever H puts all its mass to the right of k + c, or to the left of -k - c. The entry states attainment only 'by contamination at any M > c_* + k' (body 286-287). The annex proves it only for H = delta_M, plus reflection (428-430). Attainment by every contaminant concentrated on [c_* + k, infinity), or its reflection, is neither stated nor proved. Yet handbook/parts/p15/robustness-and-sensitivity-of-inference-w02b-p15-071.tex lines 114-116 cite this entry for exactly that claim.

sections.title: Robust hypothesis tests and the relation to sequential robustness

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-robust-hypothesis-testing-C005 (partial): The 'construction or argument' and 'full treatment promised by its declared status' (proved=annex:p15.huber.tv.pair) are not supplied for the k_+ direction. The theorem asserts unique k_- and k_+ (body 125-130). The proof writes existence and uniqueness only for g(k)=int(ks-p1)_+ (annex 134-144). For k_+ it says only 'The decreasing upper-transfer function int(p1-ks)_+dmu has the analogous property' (annex 145-146). No endpoint values, no strict-decrease argument and no stated reduction to the g case are written, so this is a 'similarly' that reproduces Huber's own deferral (p.1758) instead of completing it. Failure condition 'missing promised direction/case' holds. Also unwritten: the 'lower/upper region' (annex 156-167) is never defined or identified with {r<c'} and {r>c''}, the step that gives l=max{c',min(c'',r)}=q1/q0.

ED26-P15-CH-robust-sequential-endpoints-C012 (partial): Hypotheses not supplied; failure condition 'unstated assumption' holds. The entry never states its observation space. The setting it invokes allows an arbitrary measurable space (RSE body 13-14), and the chapter says no observation support was narrowed (353-354). Yet the displayed identity sup_{R in H_1} E_R N_{a,b} = E_{Q_1} N_{a,b} = (1-(3/5)^r)/(2/5) depends on X={0,1}. So do the proof steps 'its mass p at one ranges over [2/5,3/5]' and 'If no such observation has occurred by time r, the test exits at the lower boundary' (annex 487-514). With any further point x*, the chapter's convention gives score 4/5 there. The contamination delta_{x*} then gives P_R(N_{3c,b}>3)=19/125>0=P_{Q_1}(N_{3c,b}>3), so the supremum exceeds E_{Q_1}N.
